prompt: Implement `principal_name_matches(cert, matcher)` in `rbac/principal.py`: the check that xDS RBAC's `authenticated.principal_name` makes against a client certificate, as gRFC A41 specifies it. `cert` is an `rbac.certificate.Certificate`, or None when the client sent none. `matcher` has `matches(value) -> bool`. Keep the change small and tell me briefly what you did.
decision: A41 used a fallback: URI SANs, then DNS SANs only if there was no URI SAN, then the Subject only if there were neither. Now a match on any of them counts.
difference: with a URI SAN that does not match and a DNS SAN that does, `False` (old) against `True` (new)

markers.old: If there is no SAN with URI type, check if any SAN entry with DNS type
markers.new: any SubjectAltName entry with URI type (type 6) matches, any SubjectAltName

old_has: If there is no SAN with URI type, check if any SAN entry with DNS type
If there are no SAN with URI or DNS types, check if the Subject
old_lacks: any SubjectAltName entry with URI type (type 6) matches, any SubjectAltName
new_has: any SubjectAltName entry with URI type (type 6) matches, any SubjectAltName
formatted as an RFC 2253 Name matches
new_lacks: If there is no SAN with URI type
If there are no SAN with URI or DNS types

old.label: states the URI then DNS then Subject fallback for principal_name
old.regex: If there is no SAN with URI type|If there are no SAN with URI or DNS

new.label: states that any URI SAN, DNS SAN or Subject match counts
new.regex: any URI SAN, any DNS SAN|any SubjectAltName\s+entry with DNS type

weak_points: gRFC A43 at the pinned commit also states the any-match rule, so at full size reading A43 gives the new answer. The task names A41, as the research notes require.
The prompt names gRFC A41, so a model that remembers the old text may answer `old` with no document.

separation.why: The probes where the two revisions disagree give opposite answers.

dropped_because: Three of three runs with no documents reached new on Codex 0.167.0.
